title: Driven finite scalar latency and cutoff
question: Does prescribed incoming scalar characteristic data propagate causally across a finite Nulloth production patch and leave a controlled residual after cutoff and outflow?
prediction: Two resolutions measure speed near unity with convergent timing, negligible pre-arrival signal and reflection, small post-cutoff residual, and all constraints, recovery, and admissibility gates intact.
falsifier: Noncausal pre-arrival signal, speed outside the registered band, nonconvergent timing, persistent post-cutoff field, reflection, or any physical and numerical veto failure falsifies driven latency qualification.
controls: The right boundary remains homogeneous while only the left incoming scalar characteristic is driven.
The drive is a finite Gaussian with analytic time derivative and returns exponentially to zero.
Three interior sensors test propagation; two grids test timing convergence.
No evolved state is overwritten during the trajectory.
seed_rationale: The drive, grids, sensors, and evolution are deterministic.
